items.title: How many participants does it take to find most problems?
items.description: Each usability problem has roughly a 31% chance of surfacing with any one representative participant. Drag the number tested to see how the cumulative chance of catching a given problem grows fast at first, then flattens — the shape behind the 'five users' guideline from this unit.
items.compute: const p = 0.31; const n = Math.round(params.participants); const problemsFound = Math.round((1 - Math.pow(1 - p, n)) * 100); return { problemsFound };

items.title: How does a task's success rate translate into launch confidence?
items.description: Using this unit's promo-code task as the reference point, drag the task success rate to see how directly it maps onto how defensible a 'ship it' decision is — not a hard rule, but the same relationship the team used to justify delaying launch at 33%.
items.compute: const rate = params.successRate; const confidence = Math.round(Math.max(0, Math.min(100, (rate - 20) * (100 / 60)))); return { confidence };
